evidence.snippet: Per criteria outlined by the ClinGen Lumping and Splitting Working Group, we found no significant difference in phenotype, inheritance pattern OR molecular mechanism in the above-mentioned disease entities. Therefore, all the entities have been lumped under caveolinopathy.

nodes.description: Caveolin-3 is also the caveolin of cardiomyocytes. Cav3 knockout mice develop a progressive cardiomyopathy with cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, fibrosis and hyperactivated ERK1/2 signaling, and a CAV3 variant found in familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reduces cell-surface caveolin-3. No patient in a 23-patient skeletal-muscle caveolinopathy cohort had cardiac impairment, so cardiac involvement in human disease is uncommon.

evidence.reference_title: Caveolin-3 knock-out mice develop a progressive cardiomyopathy and show hyperactivation of the p42/44 MAPK cascade.
evidence.snippet: We show that p42/44 MAPK (ERK1/2) is hyperactivated in hearts derived from Cav-3 knock-out mice.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and functional analysis of a caveolin-3 mutation associated with familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: It was observed that the Thr63Ser mutation reduced the cell surface expression of caveolin-3, albeit the change was mild as compared with the LGMD mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Caveolinopathy: Clinical, histological, and muscle imaging features and follow-up in a multicenter retrospective cohort.
evidence.snippet: No patient had cardiac or respiratory impairment.

nodes.description: Mice lacking caveolin-3 lose caveolae and develop T-tubule disorganization, skeletal muscle weakness and a cardiomyopathy.
Caveolin-3 is reduced on muscle biopsy. Immunostaining is normal in a quarter or more of patients, while immunoblotting shows the reduction.

evidence.reference_title: Caveolinopathy: Clinical, histological, and muscle imaging features and follow-up in a multicenter retrospective cohort.
evidence.snippet: Whereas a quarter of patients had normal caveolin-3 immunohistochemistry results, Western blots disclosed a reduced amount of the protein.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the CAV3 gene causes partial caveolin-3 deficiency and hyperCKemia.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemistry and quantitative immunoblot analysis of caveolin-3 showed reduced expression of the protein in muscle fibers.

nodes.description: Sarcolemmal lesions fail to reseal because the MG53, dysferlin and caveolin-3 repair complex is disrupted. The dystrophin-glycoprotein complex is not the primary defect, so caveolinopathy enters the shared dystrophic chain through the membrane-repair arm. The supporting work is in cells.

evidence.reference_title: Membrane repair defects in muscular dystrophy are linked to altered interaction between MG53, caveolin-3, and dysferlin.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in Cav3 (P104L, R26Q) that cause retention of Cav3 in Golgi apparatus result in aberrant localization of MG53 and dysferlin in a dominant-negative fashion, leading to defective membrane repair.

nodes.description: Golgi-retained caveolin-3 mutants pull dysferlin and the repair protein MG53 (TRIM72) away from the sarcolemma. Dysferlin is mislocalized in muscle from patients with CAV3 variants.

evidence.reference_title: Aberrant dysferlin trafficking in cells lacking caveolin or expressing dystrophy mutants of caveolin-3.
evidence.snippet: Dysferlin is mislocalized, by an unknown mechanism, in muscle from patients with mutations in caveolin-3 (Cav-3).

nodes.description: Serum creatine kinase is raised in almost all symptomatic patients and is the only finding in isolated hyperCKemia. It is not found in every rippling muscle disease patient.

nodes.description: Most pathogenic CAV3 variants are missense changes in the N-terminal, scaffolding or membrane-spanning regions of caveolin-3. Because CAV3 has only two exons, truncating variants are not expected to trigger nonsense-mediated decay. ClinGen expects the disease mechanism to be dominant negative.

evidence.snippet: More than 50 pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants reported in humans with clinical phenotypes that form the caveolinopathy spectrum are recorded in ClinVar, most of them being missense variants.

evidence.snippet: a missense mutation in the membrane-spanning region and a micro-deletion in the scaffolding domain

nodes.description: Reported in a small number of families, sometimes without skeletal muscle disease. Not found in a 23-patient skeletal-muscle cohort.

evidence.snippet: A Thr63Ser mutation was identified in a sibling case of HCM.

evidence.reference_title: CAV3 / caveolinopathy (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: Patients with caveolinopathy show variable clinical features including, but not limited to, proximal muscle weakness, exercise-induce muscle fatigue, increased serum creatine kinase levels, percussion-induced rapid rolling muscle contractions and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM).

nodes.description: Caveolae act as a membrane reservoir that flattens to buffer tension. In patient myotubes lacking caveolae the membrane cannot buffer mechanical stress, and IL6/STAT3 signaling becomes constitutively hyperactivated. In zebrafish, a dystrophy-associated caveolin-3 mutant causes sarcolemmal damage only under vigorous muscle activity, which fits the exercise intolerance, myalgia and rhabdomyolysis seen in some patients.

evidence.reference_title: Dystrophy-associated caveolin-3 mutations reveal that caveolae couple IL6/STAT3 signaling with mechanosensing in human muscle cells.
evidence.snippet: This results in impaired regulation of the IL6/STAT3 signaling pathway leading to its constitutive hyperactivation and increased expression of muscle genes.

evidence.reference_title: Dystrophy-associated caveolin-3 mutations reveal that caveolae couple IL6/STAT3 signaling with mechanosensing in human muscle cells.
evidence.snippet: share common characteristics including mild muscle weakness, high levels of serum creatine kinase, variations in muscle fiber size, and an increased number of central nuclei

nodes.description: Skeletal muscle contracts in response to percussion, stretch or movement without accompanying electrical activity on EMG. This is the defining feature of rippling muscle disease and is common across the caveolinopathy spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in CAV3 cause mechanical hyperirritability of skeletal muscle in rippling muscle disease.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary rippling muscle disease (RMD) is an autosomal dominant human disorder characterized by mechanically triggered contractions of skeletal muscle.

evidence.reference_title: Bedside diagnosis of rippling muscle disease in CAV3 p.A46T mutation carriers.
evidence.snippet: Twenty-three patients had percussion-induced muscle mounding (PIMM) and percussion-induced rapid contractions (PIRC).

nodes.description: Mutant caveolin-3 forms abnormal oligomers that are retained in the Golgi apparatus and are excluded from caveolae. In the dominant-negative model the mutant protein also traps wild-type caveolin-3 in the Golgi. For the R26Q allele one cell study instead proposed haploinsufficiency, so the dominance mechanism may differ between variants.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic behavior of caveolin-3 R26Q, a mutant associated with hyperCKemia, distal myopathy, and rippling muscle disease.
evidence.snippet: The caveolin-3 R26Q mutant formed oligomers of a much larger size than wild-type caveolin-3 and was excluded from caveolae-enriched membranes.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic behavior of caveolin-3 R26Q, a mutant associated with hyperCKemia, distal myopathy, and rippling muscle disease.
evidence.snippet: We propose a haploinsufficiency model in which reduced levels of wild-type caveolin-3, although not rendered dysfunctional due to the caveolin-3 R26Q mutant protein, are insufficient for normal muscle cell function.

nodes.description: Caveolin-3 is reduced at the sarcolemma and caveolae are lost from the muscle fiber surface. Caveolin-3 deficiency is a sensitive and specific biopsy marker of primary caveolinopathy, although immunostaining can look normal when immunoblotting shows a reduction. With caveolin-3 absent, its scaffolding of signalling partners at the sarcolemma is lost.
